name: Superpowers
summary: External skill framework capability for disciplined software execution patterns such as planning, TDD, debugging, review, and verification.

source.notes: Registered as an available execution discipline capability. PIP-153 does not evaluate quality claims or vendor source code.

useWhen: A code, workflow, debugging, planning, review, or verification ticket benefits from a structured execution method.
A ticket explicitly asks for TDD, systematic debugging, code review handling, or branch finishing discipline.
doNotUseWhen: The task is purely strategic product judgment with no implementation workflow.
Using a skill would broaden the ticket scope or bypass repository approval gates.
routing.fallback: Use the repository execution protocols and record that no external skill workflow was used.

inputs.name: assignedTicket
inputs.description: Linear ticket scope, acceptance criteria, and validation expectations.

outputs.name: executionDiscipline
outputs.description: Structured plan, tests, review handling, or verification steps applied to the ticket.

schemas.notes: Future adapter work may normalize skill invocation logs.

allowedOperations: Apply workflow guidance inside the assigned ticket scope

cost.costDriver: Runtime or plugin availability may vary by environment.

risks.description: A broad execution workflow can accidentally turn a narrow ticket into a larger refactor.
risks.mitigation: Apply only the minimum matching skill and preserve the assigned Linear scope.

approvalTriggers: Installing or updating external skill packages
governance.dataBoundary: Do not send secrets, production data, customer data, or private evidence to external systems.
governance.sensitiveActionBoundary: Skill guidance cannot override AGENTS.md, approval gates, or the assigned ticket.
governance.loggingRequirement: Mention significant skill use in PR or Linear handoff when it materially shaped execution.
governance.updatePolicy: Update this entry when available skills, trigger rules, or operating constraints materially change.

review.reviewNotes: Pilot registry entry for disciplined engineering use only.

examples.scenario: A code ticket asks for a bug fix with tests.
examples.expectedUse: Use TDD, debugging, or verification skills as execution discipline.
examples.expectedNonUse: Do not use Superpowers to make product strategy decisions or bypass review.
